q: The QAOA (Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm) at large depth p is related to adiabatic quantum computation by:
opts: QAOA is more powerful than adiabatic QC
QAOA with parameters γ_k ≈ t_k/p, β_k ≈ (T-t_k)/p approximates the adiabatic evolution from H_B to H_C (Trotterised adiabatic evolution)
QAOA requires classical optimization; adiabatic QC does not
QAOA works only for specific graph problems
exp: For large p, QAOA with optimal parameters matches the adiabatic schedule: the angles γ_k, β_k discretise the adiabatic path from H_B to H_C. QAOA is thus the 'digital' version of adiabatic QC, with the number of layers p controlling approximation quality.
